key_insight: The paper argues that strong final-answer accuracy can hide weak structural mathematical understanding, and that “Discovery” is the main bottleneck in LLM math reasoning.
engineering_relevance: For math-capable LLM systems, targeting primitive-level reasoning during post-training can improve performance more effectively than optimizing answer accuracy alone.
method: Introduces the concept of Mathematical Primitive to probe structural understanding.
Proposes HLEI, a benchmark covering Discovery, Generation, Digestion, and Execution.
Builds ABS, a primitive-privileged self-distillation framework that transfers guided reasoning into a student model.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic diagnosis across four reasoning dimensions, showing that primitives reveal latent execution capacity and that Discovery-limited failures are especially repairable.
watch_item: Results may depend on how primitives are defined and detected, so benchmark design and annotation quality are important implementation risks.
paper_title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
